newsitem.title: CHINA: China economist calls for reduced trade barriers.
newsitem.headline: China economist calls for reduced trade barriers.

text.p: A senior Chinese economist has said China must further reduce trade barriers if it hopes to meet its economic targets into the next century, the China Business Times said on Monday.

China's foreign trade would reach $400 billion in the year 2000 and was seen rising to $800 billion by 2010, the newspaper quoted Dong Fureng, vice-chairman of the Financial and Economic Committee of the National People's Congress, or parliament, as saying. But China would have to further liberalise its economy if it wanted to meet those goals, Dong said.

China should gradually lower import tariffs and aim to free up its capital markets by doing away with restrictions on capital transfers, he said. China should look to develop markets in the former Soviet Union, eastern Europe, southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America and he said.

Beijing slashed tariffs to an average 23 percent last April and has vowed to further cut them to 15 percent by 2000. It also made its currency convertible on the current account but has set no timetable for making it fully convertible.
China notched up nearly $290 billion in foreign trade in 1996, with exports topping $151 billion and imports of nearly $139 billion. -- Beijing Newsroom (8610) 6532-1921
